headline: A Decade Later, Teen Discovers Stranger's Hidden Message in Origami Crane
meta_description: After a bicycle accident in Japan, a kind stranger folded an origami crane for 7-year-old Rika Matsuda. Ten years later, a school assignment led her to unfold…
summary_short: A stranger's act of kindness to an injured child in Japan was preserved in an origami crane—until a high school homework assignment revealed a hidden message a decade la…
body:
When Rika Matsuda was seven years old and riding her new bicycle in a Japanese park, a brake failure sent her straight into a wall. A tall, well-dressed stranger saw her fall and hurt her foot. Instead of passing by, he helped her up, took her to a water fountain to wash the wound, and lent her his phone to call her grandfather. While they waited, he taught her to fold an origami crane—carefully, beautifully—before handing it to her in silence and disappearing. Matsuda kept the white paper crane on her desk for a full decade, a quiet reminder of his kindness. Then, in high school English class, teacher Benjamin Johnson assigned students to write about an encounter with a Good Samaritan, using NPR's "My Unsung Hero" series as inspiration. The assignment triggered something in Matsuda: a sudden urge to unfold the crane and see if the man had written anything inside.

The walk home from school was hurried. When Matsuda carefully unfolded the crane in her room, she found exactly what she'd somehow sensed was there—two characters containing a well-known Japanese idiom. The message translated to: "We should treasure each time we cross paths with someone because it might never happen again." A simple reminder to cherish the moment, written by a man whose name she never knew.

"Then I realized even more how kind and how nice of a man he was," Matsuda said, reflecting on a stranger who had given her far more than first aid. He had given her a lesson in presence, wrapped in paper and preserved through time.
quick_facts: Rika Matsuda was 7 years old when she crashed her bike in a Japanese park
A stranger taught her origami while waiting for her grandfather to arrive
Ten years later, a high school NPR assignment prompted her to unfold the crane
Inside, she discovered a hidden message in Japanese about treasuring moments
Benjamin Johnson's English class used NPR's 'My Unsung Hero' as a teaching workshop
